title: Thermodynamics of Information
description: Information is physical. A demon that knows which molecules are fast can sort them and reverse entropy.

puzzle.goal: A one-bit memory holds 0 with probability p and 1 with probability 1 − p. Resetting it to a definite 0 removes its statistical entropy, which must be dumped as heat into surroundings at temperature T. Write the minimum work needed for the reset as a sum over the two states.
puzzle.name: Landauer's bound (Gibbs–Shannon entropy of a bit)
puzzle.form: - kB * T * sum ( j , 1 , 2 , p _ j * ln ( p _ j ) )
puzzle.ask: Find W/kB (in kelvin) for erasing a bit that reads 0 with probability p = @{p}, at T = @{T} K.

vars.W: minimum work to reset the bit
vars.p: probability of a state (p_j); in the numeric step, probability of 0

puzzle.method: The entropy of a distribution is −kB Σ p ln p; after the reset it is zero. The second law demands at least T ΔS of heat into the surroundings, supplied as work.
